title: What is known about 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA1LF_0LC0RE_0LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA1LF_0LC0RE_0LA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

The same cascade of counters as its relative 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA0LF_0LC0RA_0RE---: at the left end a base-3 counter N with 3-cell digits, at the right binary counters with 4-cell digits that obey the stream laws of the F02 two-word sweepers, and between them a middle part that is not decoded. The laws of N and of the binary streams are proved in Lean for every size.
verdict: The question is open. No halt in LONGRUN_STEPS steps of the C simulator; Lean proves no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide) and the laws of the outer parts of the tape for every size.
Where a halt would come from. Only F1 halts and F is entered only from D reading 1 (1LF): rarely (15 times in 108 steps), always with a 0 left of D.
What is missing. The rules of the middle part between N and the binary counters, and of the rare events.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The halting pattern never forms
claims.text: F is entered only from D reading 1, 15 times in the first 10<sup>8</sup> steps, always with a 0 left of D, so F reads 0.

claims.title: The base-3 counter N, for every size
claims.text: Read the cells left of N's low end three at a time from the head outward, 010 = 0, 110 = 1, 100 = 2, blank beyond. A visit in state A adds one; it comes back out in B without carry and in E with a carry; a carry through all digits makes the blank into a new digit 2. Proved from five token rows by induction on the number of digits.

claims.title: The binary streams, for every size
claims.text: The stream laws of the F02 sibling 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA1LF_0LC0RA_0LB--- hold for this machine: in tokens z = 00, a = 10, c = 01, a visit in state B to an a/z stream is a binary increment, a visit in state A to the counter M (digits z c, c c) adds one and wraps, sending three visits into the stream after it.

claims.title: The run uses the counter law
claims.text: In the run, the cells left of -100 are entered only in state A, and all 898,777 of those visits, from step 533,028 to step 62,483,156, are rows of the counter law; then the middle reaches -100 and N's low end moves outward. At 10<sup>9</sup> steps N fills cells -154 to about -110.

claims.title: Three parts of the tape
claims.text: The crossing profile at 10<sup>9</sup> steps: ×3 every 3 cells over -154 to about -110 (N), no pattern over -110 to -60 (the middle), ×1/2 every 4 cells over -60 to -26 (binary counters with 4-cell digits), a few hundred over -26 to 37.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator runs 10<sup>11</sup> steps from blank tape without a halt; at the end cells -202 to 47 (250 cells), 106 ones; F entered 22 times in all.

claims.title: The same middle as its relative
claims.text: As in 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA0LF_0LC0RA_0RE---, the middle grows and N's low end moves outward over time. The 54 event rules of the F02 siblings hold for this table (it differs from 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA1LF_0LC0RE_0LC--- only in F0), but their event shape never occurs (none in 10<sup>8</sup> steps).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Needed: the rules of the middle part and of the rare D1 events, then whether D can ever read 1 with a 1 to its left.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine runs a base-3 counter at its left end and binary counters at its right, both proved in Lean, with a middle part between them that nobody has decoded yet. This page runs the real machine in your browser and lists what is known.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 250 cells visited.
The base-3 counter and the binary streams, proved for every size.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
Where the time goes and the rare events start; not decoded.

sections.heading: Three parts of the tape
html: The same cascade of counters as its close relative 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA0LF_0LC0RA_0RE--- (they differ in D1, E1 and F0). The crossing profile, the number of times the head moves from each cell to the next one (c/cross.c, 109 steps), splits the tape (cells -154 to 37) into three parts:

cells at 109 stepscrossingspart
-154 to about -110×3 every 3 cells (1, 12, 119, 1,068, 9,617, 86,553, 778,985, 7,010,861, …)N, a base-3 counter, about 14 digits
-110 to -60up to 28 million, no simple patternthe middle, not decoded
-60 to -26×1/2 every 4 cells (495,734 at -58, 262,373 at -54 … 2,774 at -26)binary counters with 4-cell digits
-26 to 37a few hundred, falling to 1runs of 10 growing at rare right-end events

sections.heading: The left counter
html: The left counter N (proved). Read the cells left of N's low end three at a time, from the head outward: 010 = 0, 110 = 1, 100 = 2; blank beyond. A visit of the head in state A adds one: trailing 2s become 0s, the first other digit goes up by one, and the head comes back out in state B (no carry) or E (carry); a carry through every digit turns blank cells into a new digit 2. lean/Counter.lean proves it for every number of digits (n_inc0, n_inc1, n_inc0_carry, n_inc1_carry, n_overflow) from five token rows (lean/VisitL.lean). In the run, the cells left of -100 are entered only in state A, and all 898,777 of those visits are these rows, from step 533,028 until step 62,483,156 (c/vislaws.c); after that the middle reaches -100 and N's low end moves outward while digits are added at the top. The wall of 101s at the left end is made of N's top digits.

sections.heading: The binary streams on the right
html: The binary streams (proved). lean/Stream.lean proves for this machine the stream laws of the F02 sibling 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA1LF_0LC0RA_0LB---: in tokens z = 00, a = 10, c = 01, a visit in state B to an a/z stream is a binary increment (vb_odd, vb_even, ve_odd), a visit in state A to the counter M (digits z c = 0, c c = 1) adds one and wraps (m_inc, m_wrap). From 26 token rows mined at cell -30 (lean/VisitR.lean). This table differs from the F02 sibling 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA1LF_0LC0RE_0LC--- only in F0; the 54 F02 event rules hold for it too (events.py of the F02 folder proves them; not added here), but the F02 event shape never occurs in this run (none in 108 steps): N and M are kept apart by the middle.

sections.heading: The rare events
html: The rare events. F (whose 1 halts) is entered only from D reading 1 (1LF): 15 times in the first 108 steps, 22 by 1011, always with a 0 to the left of D, so F reads 0 and goes on with 0LA.

sections.heading: What is left
html:
• Decode the middle (cells -110 to -60 at 109 steps); it grows and eats N's low digits.
  • Write the rare D1 events as rules on the counters; can D ever read 1 with a 1 to its left?

• Direct C simulation (c/longrun.c): 1011 steps, no halt; at the end cells -202 to 47 (250 cells), 106 ones; F entered 22 times in all.
  • No macro-level accelerator: the time is spent in the undecoded middle.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 192 cells (154 left of the start, 37 right), with a density of 1s of 0.432.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: F02 engine with a different D1/F path: counters behind a growing middle
summary: Like its relative 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA0LF_0LC0RA_0RE---: a base-3 counter at the left end and binary counters at the right (both proved in Lean for every size), with an undecoded middle.
